conditions.text: Sample charges assume a recipient of similar alignment and religion requesting service at the cleric’s headquarters. Prices may be adjusted for faithful lower-level characters and raised for nonregular attendees. Travel without risk can raise charges as much as double; when at risk a cleric is likely to refuse or charge at least five times the rates. Attack spells are not listed; as a general rule specially hired spellcasters do not accompany adventures except when planned and directed by the DM.

Ditch 100 ft by 10 ft deep by 20 ft wide assumes 3–4 workers for six weeks; heavy clay doubles time. Stone fortress construction takes about one week per 10-ft cubic section; adding 50% to expenditure doubles the rate, while triple rate requires expenditure of 250% of base cost and is the stated maximum. Listed normal stone buildings take four months. Building materials are assumed on hand; quarrying, transport and architect costs are additional. Wooden buildings take about half the time of comparable stone buildings.

The stone building’s listed price includes one 1-ft stone course, 120 ft of outside walls 20 ft high, two wooden floors, two flights of stairs, roof and one wooden door; cellar excavation, ground flooring, windows, interior walls and extra doors cost extra. Each additional 1-ft course adds 10% of initial cost. A 10-ft-thick example is 500 gp plus 90%, or 950 gp. An earth rampart immediately above one side of a ditch costs 20% of the listed rampart amount.

Iron door: add or subtract 2 gp per square foot of half-inch iron altered. Secret door: no reduction for smaller portals; larger ones add 5 gp per square foot of increased size. Trap door: each additional square foot costs 1 sp. Wooden door: one square foot of added or reduced wood is 2 sp. Reinforced wooden door: each square foot alteration is 5 sp. Drawbridge: each square foot alteration is valued at 2 gp. Portcullis: adjust cost by 2 gp per square foot alteration.
The stated tunnel is dug through soft earth and floored, walled and roofed in rough stone. Hard earth increases cost by 100%; solid rock costs 500% of the listed figure.
Ballista missile cost is comparable to javelin cost; the source does not give a separate fixed price in this passage.

The listed receptacle figures are suggested costs. A specially blessed/cursed empty crystal or special leaded-glass vial is worth 2–5 gp. Combination-metal vessel capacity may be interpolated: the printed half-copper, half-silver example holds 8 vials and costs 50% of each vessel price. Fonts and basins require special order and take 4–10 (2d4+2) weeks. A defiled font/basin is smelted and remade at 20%–50% of normal figures, taking 4–6 weeks.

limitations: This is a monetary discovery census, not a source-row transcription or whole-book semantic completeness claim.
The 370-page denominator counts only the PHB and DMG PDFs. The separate DMG printed-p.175 image is a supplement and is excluded from that count.
Counts distinguish screened pages, visually screened thumbnails, and previously inventoried scoped pages; these are not interchangeable denominators.

Starting wealth, currency conversion, ordinary purchase prices, hireling wages, service fees, construction costs, spell/component costs, treasure generation, market valuations and item values are typed separately rather than treated as equivalent “prices.”
Any exact amount in discoverySummary or locatorAmountCue is a locator note only pending source-scale verification; it must not be consumed as a normalized/verified source fact.

Adjacent tables give spell level/XP rather than GP sale value; excluded after visual check.
10–60 gp weight and 600 gp weight capacity refer to physical weight/capacity, not price; visual check.
30–40 gold pieces is weight, not valuation; visual check.
Gp expressions refer to capacity/weight, not prices; visual check.
Gold-piece symbol/qualitative wealth phrases excluded; separately recorded numeric 10 gp offering and >1,000 gp behavioral threshold.

unresolved.sourceObject: Unidentified item continuing onto printed p.97
unresolved.issue: Visible sale-value formula is 1,000 gp per effective cleric level, but the object label is clipped/absent at the page break. Identity deliberately unresolved.
Tables visually identified at page/table level; row-by-row objects, values, bounds, and source matches have not been transcribed. Do not treat as complete record-level price coverage.

limitations: The source census is additional to the existing p.26 equipment table inventory; that page is not duplicated.
No whole-book visual-completeness claim: many noncandidate pages are text-screen-only and OCR/text screening can miss currency values.
Table rows and object/value pairings for the random magic-item price tables are not fully transcribed.
Bounds are deliberately whole-page and page-level only. Every recorded claim was visually associated with its source page, but fine-grained claim-specific rectangles were not measured.
The printed-p.97 continuation has a visible value but unresolved object identity.
Sale value, component value, creation price, repair fee, treasure cap, behavior threshold, weight, and starting wealth remain typed distinctly; they are not interchangeable claims.

scope.purpose: Candidate inventory of monetary prices, fees, costs, and explicit valuations found during full-page PDF text-layer census followed by visual inspection of selected original pages.
scope.coverageClaim: This is not a claim that every price in either book has been found. Search cues are fallible; unflagged/image-only or OCR-corrupted pages may contain monetary claims. Every page remains represented in the census, and unreviewed candidates stay explicit.
scope.sourcePriority: Original private PDF scan is authoritative. Text-layer/OCR cues locate candidates and do not establish source wording or absence.
scope.privacy: Original PDFs and rendered source pages remain private and are not included in the repository artifact.

screening.tool: PyMuPDF text extraction from every page of both hash-verified PDFs; page text char count recorded.
screening.candidateRule: Any page with one or more configured currency, transaction, valuation, or gem cues is a broad text candidate. This deliberately overincludes treasure tables, XP labels, carrying-weight values, and OCR noise.
limitations: Text-layer page census is not visual proof of all page content.
Image-only pages and OCR-corrupted/missed wording may contain unflagged prices.
Unreviewed cue pages are pending visual review; they are not marked as having no price.
The page-cue screen is not exhaustive and does not establish whole-book completeness.

scope.purpose: Candidate inventory of monetary prices, fees, costs, and explicit valuations found during full-page PDF text-layer census followed by visual inspection of selected original pages.
scope.coverageClaim: This is not a claim that every price in either book has been found. Search cues are fallible; unflagged/image-only or OCR-corrupted pages may contain monetary claims. Every page remains represented in the census, and unreviewed candidates stay explicit.
scope.sourcePriority: Original private PDF scan is authoritative. Text-layer/OCR cues locate candidates and do not establish source wording or absence.
scope.privacy: Original PDFs and rendered source pages remain private and are not included in the repository artifact.

screeningMethod.tool: PyMuPDF text extraction from every page of both hash-verified PDFs; page text char count recorded.
screeningMethod.candidateRule: Any page with one or more configured currency, transaction, valuation, or gem cues is a broad text candidate. This deliberately overincludes treasure tables, XP labels, carrying-weight values, and OCR noise.
limitations: Text-layer page census is not visual proof of all page content.
Image-only pages and OCR-corrupted/missed wording may contain unflagged prices.
Unreviewed cue pages are pending visual review; they are not marked as having no price.
The page-cue screen is not exhaustive and does not establish whole-book completeness.
